accuracy.evidence: Habitat facts checked against National Geographic Education entries for savanna and grassland biomes and Smithsonian National Zoo animal pages: lions, zebras, wildebeest, elephants, giraffes and cheetahs on African savanna; bison and black-tailed prairie dogs on North American prairie; prairie dogs live in colonies, give alarm calls and shelter in burrows from hawks and eagles. Herding benefits (more vigilant eyes, dilution of individual risk) follow the anti-predator literature (Pulliam 1973; Hamilton 1971). The lion-removal and spotting distances are labelled as a simple model, not real counts.

misconceptions.evidence: Addresses the documented primary errors: savanna pictured as jungle (step 0 prediction, challenge tag forest); 'alone is safer because harder to see' (herd prediction, tag alone); reading food-chain arrows as 'eats' backwards, the most common KS2 food-chain error (chain prediction, p5, tag arrow); placing prairie animals in Africa (tag place, m8); and thinking removing predators helps plants (balance prediction, m6).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagsavanna is built around open-grassland life: a two-panel savanna/prairie sorter with a lone tree, a herd of 1, 5 or 20 zebras watching a lion the child drags closer (spotting distance grows with herd size), a three-card food chain with arrows drawn to the eater, a prairie dog dragged into its burrow under a hawk, and a lions none/few/many model. flagmigrate, flagfoodweb, flagchain and flaganwhere cover journeys, webs and habitats generally, not these mechanisms.

lab_teaches.evidence: Doing comes before telling: a lone zebra notices the lion with only 2 steps to spare (miss sound), while 20 zebras notice it at 7, so safety in numbers is seen. Tapping lion first gives 'Start with the plant: grass is the producer'. Pressing 'Climb a tree' says there is no tree to climb. Removing lions shows 40 zebras and bare soil before the text explains predator–prey balance.

predictions.evidence: Five predictions with tempting wrong options the lab disproves: savanna as 'a thick forest'; a lone zebra being safer 'because it is harder to see'; zebra → lion meaning 'the zebra eats the lion'; a prairie dog hiding 'up a tall tree'; and grass growing 'taller, with nobody around' when lions leave. Each reveal names the child's pick.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Seven rotating questions (what a savanna is, why herds, which is the predator, prairie vs savanna animal, prairie dog safety, arrow meaning, lions leaving). Wrong answers map to six distinct messages: forest, alone, arrow, place, hide, balance, each naming the slip and the correct idea, with answer order rotating each turn.

readability.evidence: Kid explanation FK combined 3.8 (paragraphs 2.3 to 7.4; the higher one is the list of animal names) against the family target 5.0; adult combined 6.9 against 10.0. The curriculum words habitat, herbivore, carnivore, predator, prey and producer appear with their meanings, and sentences are short.

no_filler.evidence: Kid paragraphs teach the habitat, the animals that live there, herding as safety in numbers, and predator–prey with burrows. Adult text gives the Year 2 and Year 4 links, biome facts, five named mistakes and the lab sequence. The content gate found no filler phrases and explanation overlap with other lessons stayed under 12%.

mobile.evidence: Checked on iPhone 13 screenshots in dark and light: the two grassland panels list six and two animals without clipping, and the lone tree sits clear of the list. Twenty zebras spread over the right side with the lion to the left, the chain fits three pills and two arrows at 358 px, the burrow is a dark hole outlined in both themes, and twenty model zebras fit two rows. Every action also has a 48 px button.

accessibility.evidence: All drags have button twins: '← African savanna' and 'American prairie →' with the animal named in aria-label, herd size and 'Lion creeps closer', grass/zebra/lion chain buttons, 'Dive into the burrow' and 'Climb a tree', and the three lion buttons. Canvas aria-label and the live region update with each message. The walk gate passed axe WCAG 2.1 AA in both themes on desktop and iPhone 13.
